Public Comments
Please email all public comments to CScommission@sgch.org and include the following on the subject line
of your email: the section (Public Comment, Consent, Public Hearing, Continued Business, New Business)
and Item Number you are commenting on. The Staff will read public comments into the record for up to

discriminatory language, will not be read.

   MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 15, 2022
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Vice Chair Huerta called the special meeting of the Community Services Commission to order at
6:39 P.M. on Thursday, September 15, 2022, with Commissioners and staff in the Council
Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Commissioner Cabot.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Cheryl Anne Cabot, Catherine Cordero, Theresa Huerta
  and Ting Xie
Commissioners Absent:  None.

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Manager Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit comments, and
how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the Community Services Commission,
email all public comments to CSCommission@sgch.org.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  The Agenda Order was approved by the Commission.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT – None

3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL MINUTES

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  SEPTEMBER 15, 2022
   A motion was made by Commissioner Cabot, seconded by Commissioner
  Cordero to approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission
  Meeting for August 1, 2022.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 4-0-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CABOT, CORDERO, HUERTA, XIE
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. EMPLOYEE INTRODUCTION
  Manager Morales-Stevens introduced Amy Cortez, Recreation Supervisor.

  Public Comment: None

  B. COMMISSION REORGANIZATION
  Manager Morales-Stevens presented the item.

  Commissioner Cabot nominated Vice-Chair Huerta for Chair.
  Theresa Huerta was selected Chair by acclamation.

  Commissioner Cordero nominated Commissioner Xie for Vice Chair.
  Ting Xie was selected Vice Chair by acclamation.

  Public Comment: None

  C. DISCUSSION OF APPROVED 2022 ANNUAL WORKPLAN
  Manager Morales-Stevens presented this item.

  The Commission decided that each commissioner will oversee an item and work
  together on workplan items 1A and 1B. They are interested in collaborating with
  HEAR Commission for events. The Commission requested Ride SG information
  and data on classes, events, registrants, and resident/non-resident
  participation.

  Public Comment: None

  D. MONTHLY DEPARTMENT REPORT
COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  SEPTEMBER 15, 2022
   Manager Morales-Stevens provided the report.

  The Commission inquired about the after-school program offered at the
  elementary schools.

  Public Comment: None

5. COMMISSIONER REPORTS

  Commissioner Cabot attended a gathering where she had the opportunity to
  speak with Jennifer Tang, district representative for Assemblyman Fong. She
  received information regarding opportunities for discretionary funding for the
  Smith Park pool.

  Commissioner Cordero attended National Night Out. She enjoyed the event and
  said it was very informative.

  Vice Chair Xie also attended National Night Out.

  Public Comment: None

6. STAFF COMMENTS

  A. DATES TO REMEMBER
  Manager Morales-Stevens presented the item.

  Public Comment: None

  B. GENERAL STAFF COMMENTS
  Manager Morales-Stevens shared information regarding the Mental Wellness
  Expo, the Adult Center’s Grand Re-opening, and the backpack giveaway.

  Public Comment: None

7. ADJOURNMENT

  Chair Huerta adjourned the meeting at 7:47 p.m.

  Next regular meeting held on Monday, October 3, 2022, in the Council Chamber
  at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776, at 6:30 pm.

SUBJECT:  Community Services Commission Action Plan 2022

SUMMARY
Below is the 2022 Workplan Action Plan for the Community Services Commission to
review and discuss. This will continue to help guide the commission as they work to
complete the tasks on the Annual Workplan.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the Community Services Commission is to creatively and inclusively
explore ways in which the Community Services Department can enrich quality of life for
residents of the City of San Gabriel by providing equitable access to dynamic programs,
services and spaces that strengthen community connection and engagement.

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The Community Services Commission serves as an advisory body to the Community
Services Department and City Council, and functions as a liaison between residents and
city government. It is the responsibility of the Community Services Commission to
advocate on behalf of the San Gabriel community and to ensure that the Community
Services Department’s programs, services, spaces and events advance the Commission’s
purpose.

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  October 3, 2022

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Community Services Department Staff

BY:  Christina Alatorre, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Monthly Department Report

Youth Programs
After School Program – The After School Program at Coolidge, McKinley, Roosevelt,
Washington, and Wilson Elementary Schools are celebrating National Hispanic Heritage
Month by incorporating themed arts and crafts and activities.
Jefferson Middle School Sports – The Jefferson Middle School Volleyball and Co-Ed Flag
Football Teams have kicked off their season with their first set of games for the school
year. The Junior Varsity Football Team had their first game against Foothills Middle School
on Tuesday, September 20. Both Junior Varsity and Varsity Girls Volleyball Team had their
first games on Thursday, September 22 against Oak Avenue Middle School. The Varsity
Football Team had their first game against La Canada Middle School on Thursday,
September 29. All teams have displayed great effort and sportsmanship. The Recreation
Leaders/Coaches have done an excellent job getting players prepared for their seasons.

Contract Classes
Contract classes began the week of September 19 for the fall session of classes. Over 340
participants have registered for classes. New classes for this season include ESL and
Breakdancing.

Older Adult Programs
The grand re-opening of the City’s senior programs took place on Friday, September 23.
Approximately 150 people attended the event, which included resource panels for active
living and essential services, an art exhibit and bingo. Senior Movies are now being offered
on the second Monday of each month at the Adult Recreation Center. Technology
Tutoring will begin Wednesday, October 12.

  4-B
 Older Adult Trips have resumed for the fall. Aquarium of the Pacific was offered on
September 27 and the Temecula Winery on October 6. Whale watching at Dana Point is
offered on November 15. Most trips have sold out with approximately 45 participants per
trip.

  4-B
